findings.observation: Measured, with the numbers. The two new acceptance targets inject a store-adapter fault: a development build holds REVIEW_APP_TEST_FAULT=refuse_mark_repo_read or refuse_record_account_checks and the store then refuses that one write on every call (crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs:538-607). They are ordinary [[test]] targets in crates/openlore-review-app/Cargo.toml:170-181, so the default cargo test run includes them, and the feature's architecture brief declares ADRs: None and states no per-test, property or share budget, so no derogation ADR exists and no stated budget can be checked against. The measured cost is small: review_app_scan_store_failure 4 tests in 2.25 s and review_app_legacy_run_repos_read 6 tests in 1.66 s (libtest totals of my runs 8-10), and the whole openlore-review-app package is 311 tests in 130 s. There is also precedent the candidate did not invent: the migrate_before_commit store fault seam is already driven from a default-suite acceptance target (tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts.rs:785, support/review_app/repos_and_accounts.rs:515). So this is an authority-record gap, not a slow suite, and it is non-blocking for the Request's promises.
findings.remediation: Record the human's position once for this seam family rather than per test: either an Accepted, feature-scoped ADR cited by docs/feature/fix-repos-read-truthful/architecture.md stating that the user elected these store-fault acceptance scenarios to run in the default suite (with the measured 2.25 s / 1.66 s as its cost record, and covering the pre-existing migrate_before_commit seam), or a separate infrastructure suite the default cargo test run excludes, with its trigger and total budget. Ask the human; do not grant it in the design.

What the corrected bytes do, read rather than taken on report. The repos-read-save scenario now has three judging moments instead of two: her store refuses the mark, the run ends interrupted and her queue offers only Resume scan with no count; then when_her_store_refuses_instead restarts the same app on the same store holding REVIEW_APP_TEST_FAULT=refuse_record_account_checks (support app.rs restart_refusing, which replaces the seam value and restarts, keeping origin, store and secrets); she picks the run up, and the run she picked up must again end interrupted with only Resume scan offered and no count; only then does the store accept writes again and the last pick-up must complete with the exact count. That third moment is the stimulus my finding asked for: a resumed run meeting a refused write. It reaches crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs:555-557, the resume_scan copy of the record_checks guard, because the first scan did write a plan (the mark fault lets record_checks and the plan write through), so the pick-up resumes that frozen plan instead of starting a fresh scan.
The assertion is not vacuous and does not depend on a hard-coded expectation. when_she_picks_the_run_up now returns the status when_scan_finishes observes (pre-existing support, tests/acceptance/support/review_app/world.rs:292-313, not changed by this candidate): it presses whichever scan action the queue offers, polls /scan/status until the status is no longer "running" or 60 s pass, and returns the status it actually found - so "interrupted" is read from the product, not waited for. The preceding then_her_queue_offers_only_resume_and_claims_no_count proves only Resume scan is on the page at that moment, so the press cannot silently start a fresh scan, and that step now also checks both fresh-scan labels (Scan again and Scan my repos) and both repos-read wordings at every judging moment, which is strictly stronger than the version I reviewed. The final exact-count assertion (counts_claimed == [resumed set size]) and the subset check on the repos read before the refusal are unchanged.
The designer's reason for leaving the account-checks scenario as it was is sound on the code: record_checks runs in scan_accounts before the plan is written (scan.rs:455, the plan at ~472), so a run whose account-checks write was refused has no plan row, and a later pick-up starts a fresh scan rather than resuming - the resume guard is reachable only from the repos-read-save scenario, which is where it is now exercised. I did not reproduce the oracle reviewer's RED myself: I may not edit production code, so my evidence is the stimulus and the discriminating assertions above plus the green run, and the recorded RED (scan.rs:555-557 replaced by let _ =, failing at the oracle's line 157 with completed versus interrupted) is that reviewer's.

Paradigm bound: functional (CLAUDE.md, ADR-007); the FP rules judged are pure core / effects at the edge, total functions with every outcome in the return type, composition, and unrepresentable invalid states.
Implementation units (nine).
(1) crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs:368-392 record_checks - now total: it returns Result<(), ReviewStoreError> instead of swallowing the write with let _ =, and emits its per-account log events only after the write is stored. Cohesion kept, no new dependency, effects stay in the shell.
(2) scan.rs:455 and (3) scan.rs:556 - the two callers' guards; each ends the run Ended::with_status(ScanStatus::Interrupted), the same shape the pre-existing guards beside them use (scope lock at 463, store_moves at 468, listed_sources at 563, ResumedPlan::record at 567). No domain decision moved into effectful code; the status is a value the caller reports.
(4) scan.rs:664-692 read_planned - the mark guard returns Interrupted.after_finding(found), byte-for-byte the same treatment the unreadable source list already gets two statements above (line 678), which is exactly the precedent the Request names. The dropped StoreError reason is consistent with that precedent, so it is SSOT-consistent rather than a new silent failure; the run's Interrupted status is the loud outcome.
(5) crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs:538-607 the scan-write fault seam - ScanWriteFault (dev-only values, an empty enum in release), StoreFaults { migration, scan_write } with a const none(), the ungated pub(crate) ScanWrite naming the write a call site is making, and a pure total admits(fault, write) mirroring the existing stop_at. The release twin is match never {} over an uninhabited type, so a release binary cannot represent a fault at all - certainty by construction, not a runtime check. open_capped_with is kept as the migration-fault wrapper, so no existing caller or test had to change: reuse, not a second decider.
(6) crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs:166-171, 275-300, 328-345, 353-357 - repos_read_of(planned, read) is pure and total and returns None exactly when the run has no plan row; the discriminator lives in the store that owns the rows, not in the view. The two write methods ask admits_scan_write first and compose with and_then. One readability note, not a finding: LATEST_SCAN now holds two correlated subqueries that differ only by AND planned.status = 'read'; keeping both in one statement is what makes the pair atomic, and the comment above it says why they are read apart.
(7) crates/ports/src/review.rs:416-426 - ScanRun.repos_read: Option<usize>. A native sum type that makes "no plan to count" and "counted none" distinct and makes the conflated state unrepresentable; craftsmanship keeps a native type that already states the distinction, so no wrapper was added. Doc comment states both arms.
(8) crates/review-domain/src/views/queue.rs:307-318 and 649-656 - both render sites branch on Some; imports_only_summary composes its head by matching repos_read.map(repos_read_message), declarative, no flag. Type precision carried to the boundary.
(9) crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:41-58, 308-330 and wiring.rs:541-612 and xtask/src/check_arch.rs:1328-1345 - TestFault is a dev-only enum with an empty release twin, test_fault and store_faults are pure and total with release twins, the MigrationFault/ScanWriteFault imports are cfg-gated, and the release-build token guard gained all four new names. Dependencies point inward: the app maps its own seam names to the store's fault type at the composition root.
No Dimension 1 bias found: every added element is read by an accepted outcome (the fault seam by S1's scenarios, the Option by S2's, the token list by the release guard). No premature optimisation, no assumed problem, no abstraction without a second caller.
Test families (six).
(A) tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs - two P1 scenarios driven through the app's public HTTP port on a development build; the store, sign-in, ownership proof and scan are real, only GitHub and ATProto are doubles, so no mock sits inside the hexagon. Obligation fidelity: stored status, the queue's offered actions, the absence of any repos-read wording, the resumed completion, read_before as a subset of read_by_resume, and exactly one claimed count equal to the resumed set. Falsifier strength: counts_claimed parses the whole number in front of each wording, so an over-count that merely ends in the true number is read as the number it is; a wrong implementation that completed the run, or showed a count, or skipped an unmarked repo, fails. No tautological or zero-assertion test, no assert_called-style mirroring, no try/except around assertions, no magic oracle (every expected value is a user-visible wording or a set the scenario built).
(B) tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs - four P2 scenarios.
